content:
I must admit that I am a bit frustrated with the progress of complexity theory in CSLib. I think I have identified two main blockers for why we don't have any progress and created an issue proposing how we could remove them: https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/issues/611

The two-line summary is that I think we should define several machine models of increasing complexity and expressivity that can cross-simulate each other. I propose one (two) high-level model, but of course we can also have several.

I'm happy to answer any questions about the issue here and would love to get others' opinion on it, but we can of course also discuss on the issue itself.
Hey, could you elaborate on the difference between what you're suggesting and the existing solutions? (including those in open PRs)

Right, maybe that wasn’t so clear: what I propose is not conflicting with any existing solution. It’s more that I think that we need a high level language with resource consumption model to make substantial progress on complexity theory. I would like to continue working on such a high level language and add it to Cslib. Since it is a considerable amount of work, I first want to get some feedback if this has a chance of being accepted. Another point I wanted to stress in the issue is that there is no harm in having multiple high level languages or machine concepts and that it might even be helpful to choose a suitable language, depending on the application case.

Isn't Boole a reasonably high-level language that people are working on for Cslib?
Could you then elaborate on the difference between Boole and your vision, that would motivate working on a separate language?

The language I am proposing (RTM) is far simpler than Boole (its syntax is fully specified in the issue) and its focus is not on semantic verification but on resource consumption analysis. As far as I understand it, Boole is user facing while RTM would be a proof tool. Furthermore, I think it makes sense to have multiple models like 1-TM, k-TM, RAM, RTM, lambda calculus, etc

I'm not sure I understand what Data does, but IIUC what you're suggesting is something like the "While" language from Software Foundations, yes?
I agree multiple models are great (plus ways to convert between them), and I like "While", though it could be extended in a lot of ways (e.g. try-catch, do-while, unless, tuples, ...) which would create a ton of models which I think is slightly counterproductive.

Lots of unnecessary back and forth with unclear motivations held back the progress on this quite a bit. This proposal is, once again, reinventing that which evidently shall not be named. Also, I'm really not sure if we want to keep relying on Boole eventually coming out and being the best solution, since there has been so little information and updating about it since the announcement in late 2025
btw what does RTM stand for? I didn't see it mentioned in the issue. I tried to look it up but found only "Random TM" or "Reversible TM" which don't seem right.

I don't think I would extend such a language, the point is that we need a language that is high-level enough that we can express things like "simulate this Turing machine, count its space consumption and abort as soon as it uses more space" or "simulate this Turing machine, and as soon as it makes an oracle query, answer with this instead" or "run these two machines in parallel and stop as soon as the first of them stops".
Do you have a link to "while"?
I think Data is also important, it makes it very easy to translate procedures working on inductive data types. Take for example my implementation of "BiTape.move_right" and compare it to the one in CSLib: https://github.com/crei/cslib/blob/d7503979ef2fdba7181895c12f057e703134aaba/Cslib/Computability/Machines/RoseTreeMachine/V2/UniversalTM.lean#L210 / https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/blob/43f68e97153616714e31d90163b958f4bf4b532d/Cslib/Foundations/Data/BiTape.lean#L92

Snir Broshi schrieb:

btw what does RTM stand for? I didn't see it mentioned in the issue. I tried to look it up but found only "Random TM" or "Reversible TM" which don't seem right.

It's mostly just a placeholder. I named it RoseTreeMachine based on the data structure it operates on.
